title: Recover normalization by intersection with normalized completed branches
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume $R$ is local, with unique maximal ideal $m$, and put $H=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. There are finitely many minimal prime ideals $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $H$. Put $B_i=H/q_i$, $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)$, and let $T_i\subseteq L_i$ be the integral closure of $B_i$ in $L_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Each $B_i$ is a complete Noetherian local domain. The canonical map $R\to B_i$ is injective and induces an embedding $j_i:K\hookrightarrow L_i$. For every $x\in K$, one has $x\in N$ if and only if $j_i(x)\in T_i$ for every $i$. Equivalently, inside $\prod_iL_i$ one has $N=K\cap\prod_iT_i$, using the diagonal embedding $x\mapsto(j_i(x))_i$.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Proposition 4.7.3, printed pp. 81-82 (PDF pp. 95-96), first assertion and component construction in its proof; used in Theorem 4.10.5, printed p. 91. The component quotients and their fraction fields are taken before normalization. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $H$ is Noetherian. The ideal $m$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] gives $mH$-adic completeness and $H/mH\cong R/m$, with the first-coordinate projection as quotient map. In particular $H\ne0$. To check locality explicitly, take $h\in H$ whose first coordinate is nonzero in $R/m$. At each level $R/m^n$ a representative of $h_n$ is outside $m$, hence is a unit of the local ring $R$. Thus each $h_n$ is a unit. Their inverses are compatible, since a ring map preserves inverses; they form an inverse of $h$ in the defining inverse limit. Elements in $mH$ cannot be units, since their images in $R/m$ vanish. Therefore $H$ is local with maximal ideal $mH$, and complete for this maximal ideal.

source.place: Tags 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian) and 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); locality checked directly in the inverse limit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] to $H$ to list its distinct minimal primes as $q_1,\ldots,q_s$. The prime $mH$ contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], so $s\ge1$. Every $q_i$ is proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] to the complete Noetherian local ring $H$ and ideal $q_i$. This gives a complete Noetherian local ring $B_i=H/q_i$; it is a nonzero domain because $q_i$ is prime.

The map $R\to H$ is faithfully flat, in particular flat, by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. For each $i$ put $p_i=q_i\cap R$. Since $R$ is a domain, $(0)$ is prime and $(0)\subseteq p_i$. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to this pair and $q_i$ to obtain a prime $q_i^{\prime}\subseteq q_i$ contracting to $(0)$. Minimality of $q_i$ gives $q_i^{\prime}=q_i$, hence $p_i=(0)$. Thus $R\to B_i$ is injective. The formula $j_i(a/b)=\bar a/\bar b$ for $a,b\in R$, $b\ne0$, is consequently well-defined: fraction equality is cross multiplication, which remains valid after this ring map. Its kernel is zero because $\bar a=0$ implies $a=0$. It is the required embedding of fraction fields.

If $x\in N$, choose a monic relation $x^n+\sum_{r<n}c_rx^r=0$ with $c_r\in R$ using [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Applying $j_i$ gives the same monic relation over $B_i$ for $j_i(x)$. The same definition says that $j_i(x)\in T_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tags 00GI (definition-integral) and 00GP (definition-integral-closure); direct application of a ring map to a monic equation.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $j_i(x)\in T_i$ for every $i$, and write $x=a/b$ with $a,b\in R$, $b\ne0$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], choose for each $i$ a monic polynomial $f_i(X)=X^{d_i}+\sum_{r<d_i}c_{ir}X^r$ in $B_i[X]$, with $d_i\ge1$, annihilating $j_i(x)$. Lift each coefficient to $\widetilde c_{ir}\in H$ and set $U_i(X,Y)=X^{d_i}+\sum_{r<d_i}\widetilde c_{ir}X^rY^{d_i-r}\in H[X,Y]$. Write $a,b$ also for their images in $H$. The image of $u_i=U_i(a,b)$ in $L_i$ is $\bar b^{d_i}f_i(\bar a/\bar b)=0$. The nonzero denominator $\bar b$ exists by Step 3. Since $B_i$ injects into its fraction field, $u_i\in q_i$.

source.place: Tags 00GI (definition-integral) and 00GP (definition-integral-closure); explicit homogenization of lifted monic equations, expanding the component test in Swanson–Huneke Proposition 4.7.3.

proof.text: Put $U(X,Y)=\prod_{i=1}^sU_i(X,Y)$, $D=\sum_i d_i\ge1$, and $u=U(a,b)=\prod_i u_i$. Each minimal prime $q_i$ contains $u$, because it contains its factor $u_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] every prime of $H$ contains one of these minimal primes, and therefore contains $u$. Apply the intersection formula of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] with ideal $(0)$: $u\in\sqrt{(0)}$. The stated definition of radical gives an integer $e\ge1$ with $u^e=0$. This uses the nilradical of $H$ and does not assume $H$ reduced.

source.place: Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), parts (4) and (7); nilpotence of the product of the homogenized component equations.

proof.text: The polynomial $U(X,Y)^e$ is homogeneous of degree $M=De\ge1$, with coefficient $1$ at $X^M$. Expanding its product gives $U(X,Y)^e=X^M+\sum_{r<M}h_rX^rY^{M-r}$ for some $h_r\in H$. Evaluating at $(a,b)$ and using Step 6 gives $a^M+\sum_{r<M}h_ra^rb^{M-r}=0$ in $H$. Let $J=(a^rb^{M-r}:0\le r<M)$ be the ideal of $R$ with these displayed generators. The equation says that the image of $a^M$ belongs to $JH$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to $R\to H$, which is faithfully flat by Step 3. It gives $a^M\in J$, hence coefficients $t_r\in R$ with $a^M=\sum_{r<M}t_ra^rb^{M-r}$ in $R$.

source.place: Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), ideal contraction; explicit expansion and descent of the homogenized monic equation.

proof.text: Divide the last equality by $b^M$ in $K$: $x^M-\sum_{r<M}t_rx^r=0$. This is a monic equation over $R$, so [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] gives $x\in N$. Together with Step 4 this proves the equivalence. Since $s\ge1$ and each $j_i$ is injective, the map $K\to\prod_iL_i$, $x\mapsto(j_i(x))_i$, is injective. Under this embedding, membership in $\prod_iT_i$ is precisely membership in $T_i$ in every coordinate. The equivalence is therefore exactly the asserted intersection identity.

source.place: Tags 00GI (definition-integral) and 00GP (definition-integral-closure); division by a nonzero denominator and the set-theoretic meaning of intersection.

proof_origin.place: Explicit homogenized-polynomial proof of the component comparison in Swanson–Huneke Proposition 4.7.3, printed pp. 81–82 (author-hosted PDF pp. 95–96, read online; local PDF WANTED), using Stacks Tags 0316, 05GG, 0325, 00FR, 00MC, 00HS, 00E0 and 05CK. The argument replaces the book’s integral-ideal shorthand by coefficient lifting and ordinary ideal contraction.

The statement is true: it needs no reducedness or excellence of the completion. It holds on small cases: a field, an already complete ring, the two-branch nodal cubic y^2=x^2+x^3, x=0, and b a unit. Steps: (1) H is Noetherian by adic-completion-noetherian; mod-ideal gives mH-adic completeness and H/mH=R/m; locality is checked through unit lifts at each level. (2) There are finitely many minimal primes and s>=1 because the prime mH contains one; each B_i is complete local by complete-local-quotient applied to a proper prime. (3) Flat going-down with (0) ⊆ q_i∩R, plus minimality of q_i, gives injectivity of R->B_i for every branch, so K embeds in each L_i. (4) A monic relation over R maps to one over B_i. (5) Lifting the coefficients and homogenizing gives u_i in q_i, using that b is nonzero in B_i. (6) The product u lies in every prime, so u^e=0 by the radical formula; a nonreduced H is handled. (7) a^M lies in JH, and faithfully flat contraction R->H gives a^M in J. (8) Dividing by b^M gives a monic equation for x. proof_deps equals the union of uses; no cycle. No new nodes.
